title: unresolvedAtCompletion keeps the FIRST completion snapshot after a demote + re-complete, so it reads as current when it is historical
description:
DEFECT, filed as a record of behaviour, not as a fix. Observed by opum-cli on OCLI-181 on 2026-10-11 and REPRODUCED HERE on the dev build before filing.

WHAT HAPPENS. `unresolvedAtCompletion` (QCLI-336) is set by `task complete` from the checklist state at that completion. If the task is later moved back to an active status and completed AGAIN, the field is NOT refreshed: it still carries the FIRST completion snapshot, including the criterion text as it stood THEN. It therefore reads as a current statement about the record when it is really a historical one.

MEASURED REPRODUCTIONS (dev build, `bun src/cli/main.ts`, quest version 0.13.0, 2026-10-11):
  1. create a task with two unchecked acceptance criteria; edit to In Progress; `task complete`.
     -> unresolvedAtCompletion = {"acceptanceCriteria":[{"index":0,"text":"first criterion"},{"index":1,"text":"second criterion"}],"definitionOfDone":[]}
  2. `task demote T-1 --to "In Progress"` (Done -> active is reachable only via demote); amend BOTH criteria's text AND check them; `task complete` again.
     -> criteria are now both checked with the amended text, but unresolvedAtCompletion is UNCHANGED: still {"acceptanceCriteria":[{"index":0,"text":"first criterion"},{"index":1,"text":"second criterion"}],"definitionOfDone":[]}
     -> the field is still PRESENT after the re-completion, even though nothing is unresolved now.
  A second variant that did NOT need demote: editing a DONE task's checklist (amend text + check) also leaves the field carrying the pre-amendment snapshot -- this half is the documented write-once behaviour (QCLI-336: 'set once ... never recomputed afterward, so editing a completed task's checklist does not retroactively rewrite what was open when it closed'). The RE-COMPLETION half is the part that is not covered by that sentence: the task reached the terminal status a SECOND time and the field kept the first snapshot.

WHY IT MATTERS. A reader (or a consumer, e.g. a sweep for 'what shipped with open items') cannot tell a current statement from a stale one. The stored text can name criteria that have since been checked and reworded.

OPEN QUESTION, opum-doc's to settle (do NOT decide it here): should the field REFRESH when a task is re-completed (a new terminal transition is a new statement), or should it be documented as a write-once HISTORICAL snapshot (in which case a consumer needs a way to tell it is historical, and the QCLI-336 docblock and the `task complete` help need the re-completion case stated). Filed by the quest-cli worker at team-lead instruction; UNSTAMPED.

acceptanceCriteria.text: opum-doc's decision is recorded on whether `unresolvedAtCompletion` refreshes when a task is re-completed after a demote, or is a write-once historical snapshot -- and the code or the documentation (the QCLI-336 docblock and the `task complete` help) follows that decision

implementationNotes:
opum-doc RULING, relay 568 (2026-10-11T14:56:49Z), recorded VERBATIM as relayed by the team-lead:

"REFRESH. `unresolvedAtCompletion` describes the completion it sits beside, so a re-completion rewrites it to the current unresolved set. That set is empty when everything is now checked, and the absent-vs-empty convention stays as it is today. If quest already keeps a per-transition history (gateEvents or similar), the earlier snapshot can live there rather than in the top-level field. Do NOT add a new history mechanism for this."

NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE. This task was stamped so it is eligible for a future allowlist; the change it now describes is refresh-on-re-completion, not the defect as first filed.
finalSummary:
DEC-172 (4ae): a completion REFRESHES unresolvedAtCompletion to the current unresolved set, and a first-completion snapshot must not survive amended criteria. Any history lives in the existing per-transition records, with no new mechanism.

THE DEFECT. complete() computed the current unresolved set and then, when nothing was unresolved, returned the record UNCHANGED -- so a previous snapshot survived. A task completed, demoted back to an active status, amended (both criteria reworded AND checked) and completed again still carried the FIRST completion's text, so the field read as a current statement about the record when it was a historical one. Only the clear case was broken -- the other direction already overwrote -- which is exactly why the behaviour read as "write-once".

THE FIX, one code change. complete() now SETS the field on every completion: the computed set when there is one, and `undefined` when there is not, which removes the key the same way demoteTask clears `resolution`.

THE DOCS follow the decision. The TaskState docblock on `unresolvedAtCompletion` (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts), the `task view` help and the `task complete` help (src/application/command-help.ts), and the QCLI-336 docblock in src/cli/main.ts now all state that a COMPLETION refreshes it; that a re-completion clears it when nothing is unresolved; that editing a completed task's checklist still does not rewrite it, because only reaching the terminal status again does; and that any history lives in the record's per-transition entries with no new mechanism.

(4af) AC3 stays consistent: the change sits inside complete()'s relocation closure, so the already-Done relocation path computes the completion fields exactly as it did -- one Done shape, not two.

PROVED BOTH WAYS, both runs recorded. With the refresh IN PLACE the new test passes -- test/qcli336-unresolved-at-completion.test.ts, "a re-completion refreshes unresolvedAtCompletion, and clears it when nothing is unresolved (QCLI-479)" (1 pass, 5 expect() calls) -- pinning that demote + amend + re-complete CLEARS the field, and that a later re-completion which does leave a criterion unchecked carries THAT criterion's reworded text rather than the first snapshot's. With the refresh REMOVED (restoring `unresolved === undefined ? withSummary : ...`) the same test goes RED at the clear assertion, receiving the stale first snapshot ({acceptanceCriteria: [{index:0,text:"first criterion"},{index:1,text:"second criterion"}], definitionOfDone: []}); the control was reverted, and the whole file then reads 5 pass / 0 fail.

Verified: bun run check exits 0 on the declared bun 1.4.2.
